'''Sidney Holgate''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE}} (9 September 1918 – 17 May 2003) was a British mathematician and [[academic administrator]].

==Biography==
Holgate was born on 9 September 1918 in [[Hucknall]], Nottinghamshire, England.<ref name="times" /> He was educated at [[Henry Mellish School and Specialist Sports College|Henry Mellish School]]. He won a scholarship to [[Hatfield College, Durham]], where he studied mathematics and eventually became "[[senior man]]" (i.e. president of the [[junior common room]]).<ref name="times">{{cite web|title=Sidney Holgate|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/cricket/article/sidney-holgate-pcnf260tlg5|website=The Times|access-date=11 March 2018|language=en|date=10 June 2003}}</ref> He was also President of the [[Durham Union]] for [[Michaelmas term]] of 1940.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Campbell |first1=P. D. A. |title=A Short History of the Durham Union Society |date=1952 |publisher=Durham County Press |page=17}}</ref> He graduated with a [[first class honours]] [[Bachelor of Arts]] (BA) degree in 1940.<ref name="WWW">{{cite web |title=Holgate, Dr Sidney, (9 Sept. 1918–17 May 2003), Founder Master of Grey College, University of Durham, 1959–80; Member, Academic Advisory Committee, Open University, 1969–81 (Vice-Chairman, 1972–75; Chairman, 1975–77) |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U20487 |website=Who Was Who |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=4 August 2026 |doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U20487 |date=1 December 2007}}</ref> He remained at Durham to train as a teacher and competed the Diploma in the Theory and Practice of Teaching (DThPT) in 1941.<ref name="WWW" /> 

Following the outbreak of the [[Second World War]], Holgate was found unacceptable for wartime service on medical grounds.<ref name="times" /> After graduation, he instead taught for a year at [[Nottingham High School]].<ref name="times" /> However, in 1942, he returned to Durham as a [[lecturer]] to teach mathematics and navigation to Royal Air Force aircrew cadets.<ref name="times" /><ref name="WWW" /> As such, he was commissioned in the [[Royal Air Force Volunteer Reserve (Training Branch)]], serving from 1942 to 1945.<ref name="WWW" /> During this time he continued his studies and completed a [[Master of Arts]] (MA) degree in 1943.<ref name="WWW" /> He also undertook research "on the application of [[complex variables]] to problems in elasticity" and completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) degree in 1945.<ref name="times" />

In 1946, Holgate became secretary of the [[Colleges of Durham University|Durham Colleges]]; in that role, he was the senior administrator of the University's colleges in the city of Durham, excluding King's College in Newcastle.<ref name="obit – Durham University" /> He was then [[Master (college)|master]] of [[Grey College, Durham]] from its foundation in 1959.<ref name="obit – Durham University" /> Grey College was the first postwar college established in Durham, and he oversaw its development from construction onwards.<ref name="times" /> He additionally served as [[pro-vice-chancellor]] and sub-warden of [[Durham University]] from 1964 to 1969.<ref name="times" /><ref name="obit – Durham University">{{cite web|title=Dr Sidney Holgate 1918–2003: First Master of Grey College|url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/news/newsitem/?itemno=3377|work=News|publisher=Durham University|accessdate=26 August 2024|archivedate=10 December 2007|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071210062629/https://www.dur.ac.uk/news/newsitem/?itemno=3377}}</ref> He retired in September 1980, and was succeeded as master of Grey College by [[Eric Halladay]].<ref name="DUG">{{cite journal |title=Appointments: Head of Houses |journal=Durham University Gazette |volume=XXV |issue=2 |date=31 January 1981 |pages=4-6 |url=https://reed.dur.ac.uk/xtf/view?docId=bookreader/DU_Gazettes/DUGazette25_2/dg252METS.xml#page/4/mode/2up |access-date=23 August 2026 |publisher=[[Durham University]]}}</ref>

In addition to his full-time work at Durham University, Holgate was involved with the [[Open University]] (OU) from its foundation until his retirement.<ref name="times" /> He was a member of its academic advisory committee from 1969 to 1981, serving as its vice-chair from 1972 to 1975 and its chair from 1975 to 1977.<ref name="WWW" /> The OU awarded him an honorary [[Doctor of the University]] (DUniv) degree in 1980.<ref name="WWW" />

In the [[1981 New Year Honours]], Holgate was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE).<ref name="LG 30 December 1980">{{London Gazette |issue= 48467 |date= 30 December 1980 |page= 8 |supp= y |city= |title= |quote=}}</ref>

Holgate married Isabel "Belle" Armorey in 1942.<ref name="WWW" /> They did not have any children.<ref name="times" /> He died on 17 May 2003, aged 84.<ref name="times" /> He had been living in a nursing home in Durham at the time of his death.<ref name="LG 2 July 2003">{{London Gazette |issue= 56988 |date= 2 July 2003 |page= 8231 |supp= |city= |title= |quote=}}</ref>
